theorySlides.title: ES6+ Modern Syntax 🚀
theorySlides.content:
Key ES6+ features:
• Destructuring
• Spread operator
• Rest parameters
• Default parameters
• Template literals

theorySlides.title: Destructuring
theorySlides.content: Extract values from arrays and objects.

theorySlides.title: Template Literals 📝
theorySlides.content:
Powerful string formatting:
• Use backticks ` instead of quotes
• Embed expressions with ${}
• Multi-line strings built-in
• Tagged templates for custom processing

theorySlides.title: Default Parameters 🎯
theorySlides.content:
Set default values for function parameters:
• Defaults used when argument is undefined
• Can use expressions as defaults
• Earlier params available in later defaults

theorySlides.title: Enhanced Object Literals ⚡
theorySlides.content:
Shorter syntax for objects:
• Property shorthand
• Method shorthand
• Computed property names

questions.question: What does const [a, b] = [1, 2] do?
questions.explanation: Array destructuring assigns array elements to variables.

questions.question: Which syntax is correct for template literals?
questions.explanation: Template literals use backticks ` and ${} for interpolation.

questions.question: What happens when you call greet() with function greet(name = "World")?
questions.explanation: Default parameters are used when arguments are undefined or not provided.

questions.question: What is { name, age } shorthand for?
questions.explanation: Property shorthand creates properties with variable names and values.

codingChallenge.title: Destructure User
codingChallenge.hint: Complete the line: const { name, email } = user;

theorySlides.title: Spread Operator ... 📤
theorySlides.content:
Spread expands elements:
• Combine arrays
• Clone objects
• Pass arguments

theorySlides.title: Examples
theorySlides.content: Spread in action.

theorySlides.title: Object Spread Deep Dive 🔄
theorySlides.content:
Object spread for immutable updates:
• Clone objects without mutation
• Override specific properties
• Merge multiple objects
• Order matters for overrides!

theorySlides.title: Rest Parameters in Functions 📥
theorySlides.content:
Collect remaining arguments:
• Must be last parameter
• Creates a real array (not arguments object)
• Works with destructuring

theorySlides.title: Spread vs Rest Comparison 🎯
theorySlides.content:
Same syntax, different contexts:
• Spread: Expands (unpacks)
• Rest: Collects (packs)
• Position determines behavior

questions.question: What is rest parameters?
questions.explanation: Rest (...args) collects remaining arguments into array.

questions.question: What does { ...obj1, ...obj2 } produce if both have property "x"?
questions.explanation: In object spread, later properties override earlier ones.

questions.question: Where must rest parameter appear in function signature?
questions.explanation: Rest parameter must be the last parameter in a function.

questions.question: What does const [a, ...b] = [1, 2, 3] assign to b?
questions.explanation: Rest in destructuring collects remaining elements into an array.

codingChallenge.title: Merge Arrays
codingChallenge.description: Merge two arrays with spread operator.

theorySlides.title: Functional Array Methods 🔧
theorySlides.content:
Transform arrays without mutation:
• **map**: Transform each element
• **filter**: Keep matching elements
• **reduce**: Combine to single value
• **find**: Get first match

theorySlides.title: Chaining Methods
theorySlides.content: Chain for powerful transformations.

theorySlides.title: find() and findIndex() 🔍
theorySlides.content:
Search for single elements:
• find(): Returns first matching element
• findIndex(): Returns index of first match
• Returns undefined/-1 if not found
• Stops searching after first match

theorySlides.title: some() and every() ✅
theorySlides.content:
Test array conditions:
• some(): At least one matches (OR)
• every(): All must match (AND)
• Return boolean values
• Short-circuit when result is determined

theorySlides.title: includes() and flat() 📋
theorySlides.content:
More useful array methods:
• includes(): Check if element exists
• flat(): Flatten nested arrays
• flatMap(): Map then flatten

questions.question: What does filter() return?
questions.explanation: filter() returns new array with elements passing the test.

questions.question: What does find() return if no element matches?
questions.explanation: find() returns undefined when no element satisfies the condition.

questions.question: What does [1,2,3].some(n => n > 2) return?
questions.explanation: some() returns true because at least one element (3) is greater than 2.

questions.question: What does [1,2,3].every(n => n > 0) return?
questions.explanation: every() returns true because all elements are greater than 0.

theorySlides.title: Promises ⏳
theorySlides.content:
A Promise represents future value.

States:
• **pending**: Initial
• **fulfilled**: Success
• **rejected**: Error

theorySlides.title: Creating Promises
theorySlides.content: Create and chain promises.

theorySlides.title: Promise.all() - Parallel Execution 🚀
theorySlides.content:
Run multiple promises in parallel:
• All must succeed for success
• Fails fast on first rejection
• Results in same order as input
• Great for independent async tasks

theorySlides.title: Promise Error Handling 🛡️
theorySlides.content:
Proper error handling strategies:
• .catch() for chain errors
• reject() for explicit failures
• Error propagation through chain
• finally() for cleanup

theorySlides.title: Promise.allSettled() & Promise.race() 🏁
theorySlides.content:
More Promise combinators:
• allSettled(): Wait for all, never rejects
• race(): First to settle wins
• any(): First to fulfill wins

questions.question: What does .catch() handle?
questions.explanation: .catch() handles rejected promises and errors.

questions.question: What happens if one promise in Promise.all() rejects?
questions.explanation: Promise.all() fails fast - it rejects immediately when any promise rejects.

questions.question: What does .finally() do?
questions.explanation: finally() always executes after the promise settles, regardless of outcome.

questions.question: Which method waits for all promises and never rejects?
questions.explanation: Promise.allSettled() waits for all promises and returns their results, never rejects.

codingChallenge.title: Create Promise
codingChallenge.description: Create promise that resolves with "Hello" after delay.

theorySlides.title: Async/Await ✨
theorySlides.content:
Write async code like sync:
• **async**: Makes function return Promise
• **await**: Pauses until Promise resolves
• Use try/catch for errors

theorySlides.title: Example
theorySlides.content: Clean async code.

theorySlides.title: Try/Catch Error Handling 🛡️
theorySlides.content:
Proper error handling with async/await:
• Wrap await calls in try/catch
• Catch specific error types
• Always handle errors gracefully
• Can re-throw for higher-level handling

theorySlides.title: Parallel Await with Promise.all 🚀
theorySlides.content:
Run async operations in parallel:
• Sequential await is slow
• Promise.all() runs in parallel
• Use when requests are independent
• Significant performance improvement

theorySlides.title: Advanced Async Patterns 🎯
theorySlides.content:
Common async patterns:
• Async loops (for...of with await)
• Retry logic
• Timeout handling
• Async IIFE

questions.question: Where can you use await?
questions.explanation: await can only be used inside async functions.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using try/catch with async/await?
questions.explanation: try/catch provides clean, synchronous-style error handling for async code.

questions.question: How do you run multiple awaits in parallel?
questions.explanation: Promise.all() runs multiple promises in parallel and awaits all results.

questions.question: What does an async function always return?
questions.explanation: Async functions always return a Promise, even if you return a plain value.
